title: Give the Specialist a Smaller Tool Surface
tagline: The capability a sub-agent must not have is the one it should not be given.

story.problem: Research was delegated with eve's built-in `agent` tool, which runs a copy of the ROOT agent — same instructions, same tools, including `send_outreach`. Nothing looked wrong and the plans were good, but the capability to email a stranger was inherited rather than granted, so a research child was one bad inference away from using it.
story.solution: Move research into a declared subagent at `agent/subagents/scout`, whose entire tool surface is web search plus `record_vendor`. Declared subagents inherit nothing, so the disabled shell tools and the observability hook are re-authored under that directory. Then shadow eve's built-in `agent` tool with an authored refusal, because `disableTool()` does not cover a built-in and a rule in a prompt is not a control.
story.outcome: The capability is absent rather than forbidden: research and outreach never share a context. A later production session showed the planner still reaching for both delegation paths — 10 `scout` calls and 3 `agent` calls in one session — which is why the built-in is shadowed rather than merely discouraged.

prerequisites: Node 24.x and this repository checked out — the commands inspect the real agent, not a sample
eve ^0.24.4; `eve build` writes the `.eve/agent-summary.json` manifest the checks read
NEBIUS_API_KEY in .env.local if you intend to run the agent rather than only inspect its tool surface
Familiarity with agent/lib/models.ts — planner and scout are separate roles on purpose

quickstart.clone: git clone https://github.com/jaredwerba/vendor-scout.git && cd vendor-scout && npm install
quickstart.configure: Set NEBIUS_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY in .env.local. The tool-surface checks in this recipe need no keys; npm run eval:scout does.
quickstart.run: npm run build:eve && jq -r '.tools[].name' .eve/agent-summary.json && grep -L disableTool agent/subagents/scout/tools/*.ts
